subject: Clarify: how long-context streaming and token rounding affect charges
messages:
From: Ethan Lee <ethan.lee@qoptech.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Question on billing for long streaming sessions / context length

Hi Kimberly,

Quick question as we finalize the SOW: our pipeline makes heavy use of long-context summaries (30–40k tokens) and we stream partial outputs back to the client every 2–3 seconds. We want to understand two things for pricing/forecasting:

1) How are tokens counted for streaming sessions with very long context windows? Specifically: if we open a streaming call where the full context is 35k tokens but the incremental response is 120 tokens every chunk, do you charge for the full 35k on each request or for the new tokens generated per chunk?

2) Rounding/minimums: does Redwood round up to a per-request minimum (e.g., 1k token floor) or use per-token metering with fractional aggregation across the billing period? Any example math would help — we need to forecast burn for our committed capacity.

We have an initial pilot commitment in the SOW for 10M tokens/month and are evaluating whether to add a long-context add-on.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if easier.

—Ethan
Account Lead, QopTech

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Question on billing for long streaming sessions / context length

Hi Ethan — thanks for the clear questions and for attaching the SOW. Short answers up front:

- We bill based on tokens processed by the model at inference time (both input and output). For streaming, we charge for the tokens that are actively processed for each model inference call — that includes any new input tokens and any reused KV/prefix tokens that the runtime needs to evaluate.
- We do not automatically charge the full 35k repeatedly if the runtime is able to honor a warm KV cache / prefix reuse pattern; in that case you’ll only pay for incremental tokens plus any cache re-materialization cost.
- For minimums/rounding: we use per-token metering with a 1,024-token quantum for final invoice aggregation (we round each call up to the nearest 1,024 tokens when generating invoice line-items). However, we also aggregate across the billing period and apply residual smoothing so you don’t double-pay small fragments across many calls.

I realize that’s a lot — I attached an example invoice and a short worked example below. If helpful we can propose a pilot credit to cover the uncertainty while you evaluate long-context patterns.

Example (simplified):
- Single streaming call with 35k context where runtime reuses KV cache after the first call: First call processes 35k input + 300 tokens output => rounded up to 36,352 (35k + 300 ~= 35,300 => rounded up to 36,352). Subsequent incremental chunks only bill for the new 120 generated tokens plus any ~64-token cache re-materialization overhead if cache windows shift; each chunk gets rounded up individually but monthly smoothing reduces net overhead.

I’ll follow up internally on the smoothing and sample math and send a short proposal for a pilot credit.

Best,

Ethan / Maya — thanks for the patience while we pulled the numbers together. Below is a concise summary plus the pilot credit proposal attached.

Summary of billing behavior (final):
- Metering basis: per-token (input + output) at inference evaluation time. The runtime charges for tokens that the model actually ingests to produce each chunk/response.
- Cache reuse: when the runtime can reuse a warm KV/prefix cache, you are charged only for incremental tokens plus any small re-materialization cost when windows shift.
- Rounding quantum: we round up each call to the nearest 1,024-token quantum when creating invoice line items, but we aggregate usage across the billing period and apply residual smoothing so small repeated round-ups are amortized. Practically, this means the rounding overhead is most visible for many tiny calls; for long streaming where you generate larger chunks (100–500 tokens) it’s less material.
- Discounting / committed tokens: your committed 10M token plan gives you the committed-rate break on the first 10M tokens. Overage is billed at standard rate; however for this pilot we are prepared to apply a temporary 10% discount on overage above 10M for the first two months (cap $15k) while you validate long-context patterns.

Worked example (monthly, simplified):
- Baseline: 10M committed tokens/month (applied at committed rate).
- Pilot month usage (example): 12.4M tokens total processed (input+output).
  - Committed bucket: 10,000,000 at committed price.
  - Overage: 2,400,000 at standard price, minus 10% pilot discount = billed as 2,160,000 equivalent tokens (pricing adjusted).
  - Rounding overhead: raw rounding math added ~0.4% in this pattern after monthly smoothing (~9.6k tokens).

Pilot credit proposal (attached):
- We’re proposing a one-month pilot credit that covers up to 50% of estimated incremental overage rounding overhead (capped at $5k) + the 10% overage discount above. Aim: remove uncertainty while you instrument KV reuse in prod.

Next steps:
1) If you agree, we’ll add the pilot credit and updated payment terms to the SOW and issue a revised invoice.
2) We’ll run a short telemetry check during your first week of integration to confirm cache hit rates and provide a re-estimate.

If you want more granular math, Ben attached three invoice simulations (warm reuse, full resend, partial re-materialization). Vivek included the KV overhead assumptions used.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
